official.description_text:
Postdoc in AI, Learning, and Control for Sustainable Food Systems
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
Food systems contribute to major societal challenges, including chronic disease, greenhouse gas emissions, environmental degradation, rising economic costs. Emerging food innovations, combined with digitalization and automation, are transforming agro-food value chains by changing how we produce, process, package, supply, and distribute food. At the same time, dietary choices are recognized as critical determinants of human health and environmental sustainability. The transition toward sustainable food systems requires addressing complex challenges spanning physical/communication infrastructures, individual behavior and social norms, and policy frameworks.
We are looking for postdocs with a strong background and interest in networked control systems, mathematics, machine learning, and their application to food systems. The project will focus on the analysis and control of food systems, including questions such as how AI-based methods can be used to (1) model and predict complex decision-making behavior across interconnected actors; (2) capture interactions among producers, consumers, policymakers, and technology providers in evolving food ecosystems; (3) design interventions that promote sustainable diets, reduce environmental impact, and improve system resilience.
The duties of the postdoc include:
Conduct innovative research within the scope of the postdoc position at
KTH FOOD
Publication of papers in high-quality journals, including leading perspective articles on sustainability of food innovations; present research at conferences
Initiate collaboration with other postdocs at KTH FOOD, as well as within relevant networks both nationally and internationally within academia, industry, government, or nonprofits.
Initiate and participate in funding applications to relevant calls, nationally and internationally.
Academic service, such as participating in KTH Food Centre and departmental meetings and seminars; contributing to outreach and public engagement activities.
Collaboration with one of the other themes (
Sustainable Food production
,
Functional Food Products and Health
,
Value Chains and Consumption
,
Circular Food Processes
) is expected.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Applicants must hold a doctoral degree in Electrical Engineering, Automatic Control, Applied Mathematics, or a similar field.
The successful applicants are required to have research expertise with an outstanding research and publication record; well-developed analytical and problem-solving skills.
We are looking for strongly motivated individuals who can work well both independently and collaboratively.
A good command of English orally and in writing is required to present and publish research results.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

ai.summary: A postdoctoral position in AI, learning, and control applied to sustainable food systems. The research focuses on networked systems, complex decision-making modelling, and AI-based interventions across producers, consumers, and policymakers within agro-food value chains.

thematic_fit.rationale: The position centres on food systems, sustainability, and policy-level behaviour change across stakeholders—domains unrelated to human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, or collaborative immersive systems. While the posting mentions 'behaviour' and 'decision-making', these are addressed through control theory and AI modelling, not through human perception, presence, embodiment, or immersive interaction. No XR or immersive systems component.

methodological_fit.rationale: The posting emphasizes networked control systems, machine learning, optimization, and mathematical modelling. The researcher has beginner-level Python, intermediate quantitative research, but no background in control theory, optimization, or systems dynamics. The posting explicitly requires 'strong background and interest in networked control systems, mathematics, machine learning'—none of which are strengths in the researcher's profile. User-studies and experimental-design skills do not align with control systems analysis or large-scale behavioural modelling.

growth_value.rationale: Accepting this position would require substantial retraining in control theory, systems dynamics, and applied machine learning. These are generic computational skills with no direct relevance to spatial cognition, immersive learning, or collaborative immersive systems research. The researcher would not close gaps in their target capability areas; instead, they would acquire distant technical expertise.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a top-tier institution in Sweden (priority region). The position is 2 years, allowing time to publish and establish a post-doctoral profile. However, the research group (KTH FOOD, networked systems and AI) is not part of human-centred XR, HCI, or immersive systems research communities. Publishing in food systems and control theory would not build reputation within the researcher's target field. Post-doctoral career momentum would lead toward smart systems, smart cities, or sustainability research—not immersive systems.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Posting requires doctoral degree by the time of employment decision. Thesis must be completed and degree formally conferred before start.
Posting states 'doctoral degree obtained within the last three years' is preferred—researcher's MSc by Research will likely not qualify as a doctoral degree.
Posting requires 'strong background in mathematical tools'—researcher's background is primarily in design and HCI, not mathematics or control theory.
risks: Severe domain misalignment: food systems, sustainability policy, and control engineering bear no thematic relation to immersive systems or spatial learning.
Supervisor group (KTH FOOD, systems & control) has no apparent track record in human-centred XR or HCI.
Machine learning and control theory skills acquired would have low transferability to human-centred immersive systems research.
Two-year contract in a non-target domain would delay or redirect career momentum toward human-centred XR PhD.
Publications and network established would be in food systems and control engineering, not HCI or XR communities.
No pathway to doctoral positions in human-centred XR; instead, this leads toward applied AI for sustainability.
